lines.raw: Lesson 2: PHI and Who Must Protect It.
lines.say: Lesson 2: P H I and Who Must Protect It.

lines.raw: What counts as protected health information, the 18 identifiers, and who HIPAA applies to.
lines.say: What counts as protected health information, the 18 identifiers, and who HIPAA applies to.

lines.raw: In this lesson you will:
lines.say: In this lesson you will:

lines.raw: Define PHI in plain words.
lines.say: Define P H I in plain words.

lines.raw: List the 18 HIPAA identifiers.
lines.say: List the 18 HIPAA identifiers.

lines.raw: Tell covered entities from business associates.
lines.say: Tell covered entities from business associates.

lines.raw: Explain what a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) is.
lines.say: Explain what a Business Associate Agreement (B A A) is.

lines.raw: What exactly is protected?
lines.say: What exactly is protected?

lines.raw: HIPAA does not protect every piece of health information in the world.
lines.say: HIPAA does not protect every piece of health information in the world.

lines.raw: It protects **PHI**: Protected Health Information.
lines.say: It protects P H I: Protected Health Information.

lines.raw: Information becomes PHI when two things come together: something about a person's **health, care or payment for care**, and something that can **identify** who that person is.
lines.say: Information becomes P H I when two things come together: something about a person's health, care or payment for care, and something that can identify who that person is.

lines.raw: The PHI test.
lines.say: The P H I test.

lines.raw: PHI equals health information plus something that identifies the person (held by a covered entity or business associate).
lines.say: P H I equals health information plus something that identifies the person (held by a covered entity or business associate).

lines.raw: For example: "A patient had strep throat" is not PHI.
lines.say: For example: "A patient had strep throat" is not P H I.

lines.raw: "Emily Carter, member M1001, had strep throat on 10 March 2025" is PHI.
lines.say: "Emily Carter, member M 1 0 0 1, had strep throat on 10 March 2025" is P H I.

lines.raw: Like an OPD register in Nepal.
lines.say: Like an O P D register in Nepal.

lines.raw: A hospital OPD register lists each patient's name, age, address and complaint.
lines.say: A hospital O P D register lists each patient's name, age, address and complaint.

lines.raw: Tear off the name and address column and the page says only "35-year-old woman, fever".
lines.say: Tear off the name and address column and the page says only "35-year-old woman, fever".

lines.raw: Keep the names and the page tells the whole hospital who was sick with what.
lines.say: Keep the names and the page tells the whole hospital who was sick with what.

lines.raw: The **combination** is what makes it sensitive.
lines.say: The combination is what makes it sensitive.

lines.raw: PHI.
lines.say: P H I.

lines.raw: Protected Health Information: identifiable health, care or payment information held by a covered entity or business associate.
lines.say: Protected Health Information: identifiable health, care or payment information held by a covered entity or business associate.

lines.raw: Paper, spoken and electronic forms all count.
lines.say: Paper, spoken and electronic forms all count.

lines.raw: ePHI.
lines.say: ePHI.

lines.raw: Electronic PHI: PHI stored or sent electronically, in databases, files, emails and so on.
lines.say: Electronic P H I: P H I stored or sent electronically, in databases, files, emails and so on.

lines.raw: The Security Rule is about ePHI.
lines.say: The Security Rule is about ePHI.

lines.raw: Individually identifiable.
lines.say: Individually identifiable.

lines.raw: Identifies the person, or gives a reasonable basis to identify them.
lines.say: Identifies the person, or gives a reasonable basis to identify them.

lines.raw: Payment data is health data.
lines.say: Payment data is health data.

lines.raw: A claim with **only** a member ID, a date and a dollar amount is still PHI.
lines.say: A claim with only a member I D, a date and a dollar amount is still P H I.

lines.raw: It shows that a person got care on that day.
lines.say: It shows that a person got care on that day.

lines.raw: Claims, eligibility files and pharmacy fills are all PHI.
lines.say: Claims, eligibility files and pharmacy fills are all P H I.

lines.raw: The 18 identifiers.
lines.say: The 18 identifiers.

lines.raw: HIPAA lists **18 types of identifiers**.
lines.say: HIPAA lists 18 types of identifiers.

lines.raw: They matter most when you want to make data **de-identified** (taught in lesson 6): every one must be removed.
lines.say: They matter most when you want to make data de-identified (taught in lesson 6): every one must be removed.

lines.raw: They cover the patient and also their **relatives, employer and household members**.
lines.say: They cover the patient and also their relatives, employer and household members.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: 1. Identifier: Names. Example from Emily's records: Emily Carter.
lines.say: 1. Identifier: Names. Example from Emily's records: Emily Carter.

lines.raw: 2. Identifier: Geographic areas smaller than a state: street address, city, county, ZIP code (the first 3 digits of a ZIP may stay if that area has more than 20,000 people). Example from Emily's records: Street address, Austin, ZIP code.
lines.say: 2. Identifier: Geographic areas smaller than a state: street address, city, county, Z I P code (the first 3 digits of a Z I P may stay if that area has more than 20,000 people). Example from Emily's records: Street address, Austin, Z I P code.

lines.raw: 3. Identifier: All parts of dates (except the year) linked to the person: birth, admission, discharge, death, service dates. Ages over 89 must be grouped as "90 or older". Example from Emily's records: Born 1990-08-14, seen 2025-03-10.
lines.say: 3. Identifier: All parts of dates (except the year) linked to the person: birth, admission, discharge, death, service dates. Ages over 89 must be grouped as "90 or older". Example from Emily's records: Born 1990-08-14, seen 2025-03-10.

lines.raw: 4. Identifier: Telephone numbers. Example from Emily's records: Her mobile number.
lines.say: 4. Identifier: Telephone numbers. Example from Emily's records: Her mobile number.

lines.raw: 5. Identifier: Fax numbers. Example from Emily's records: A clinic fax with her name on it.
lines.say: 5. Identifier: Fax numbers. Example from Emily's records: A clinic fax with her name on it.

lines.raw: 6. Identifier: Email addresses. Example from Emily's records: Her personal email.
lines.say: 6. Identifier: Email addresses. Example from Emily's records: Her personal email.

lines.raw: 7. Identifier: Social Security numbers. Example from Emily's records: Her SSN.
lines.say: 7. Identifier: Social Security numbers. Example from Emily's records: Her S S N.

lines.raw: 8. Identifier: Medical record numbers. Example from Emily's records: Lakeside General Hospital's record number for her.
lines.say: 8. Identifier: Medical record numbers. Example from Emily's records: Lakeside General Hospital's record number for her.

lines.raw: 9. Identifier: Health plan beneficiary numbers. Example from Emily's records: Member ID `M1001`, insurance card ID `48291307-01`.
lines.say: 9. Identifier: Health plan beneficiary numbers. Example from Emily's records: Member I D M 1 0 0 1, insurance card I D 4 8 2 9 1 3 0 7 dash 0 1.

lines.raw: 10. Identifier: Account numbers. Example from Emily's records: Her hospital billing account.
lines.say: 10. Identifier: Account numbers. Example from Emily's records: Her hospital billing account.

lines.raw: 11. Identifier: Certificate and licence numbers. Example from Emily's records: Her driving licence number.
lines.say: 11. Identifier: Certificate and licence numbers. Example from Emily's records: Her driving licence number.

lines.raw: 12. Identifier: Vehicle identifiers and serial numbers, including number plates. Example from Emily's records: Her car number plate.
lines.say: 12. Identifier: Vehicle identifiers and serial numbers, including number plates. Example from Emily's records: Her car number plate.

lines.raw: 13. Identifier: Device identifiers and serial numbers. Example from Emily's records: Serial number of an implant or medical device.
lines.say: 13. Identifier: Device identifiers and serial numbers. Example from Emily's records: Serial number of an implant or medical device.

lines.raw: 14. Identifier: Web URLs. Example from Emily's records: A link to her personal page.
lines.say: 14. Identifier: Web U R L's. Example from Emily's records: A link to her personal page.

lines.raw: 15. Identifier: IP addresses. Example from Emily's records: Her IP when she logs in to the insurer's website.
lines.say: 15. Identifier: I P addresses. Example from Emily's records: Her I P when she logs in to the insurer's website.

lines.raw: 16. Identifier: Biometric identifiers, such as finger and voice prints. Example from Emily's records: Her fingerprint.
lines.say: 16. Identifier: Biometric identifiers, such as finger and voice prints. Example from Emily's records: Her fingerprint.

lines.raw: 17. Identifier: Full-face photos and similar images. Example from Emily's records: A photo on her ID card.
lines.say: 17. Identifier: Full-face photos and similar images. Example from Emily's records: A photo on her I D card.

lines.raw: 18. Identifier: Any other unique identifying number, characteristic or code. Example from Emily's records: Claim number `23098908`.
lines.say: 18. Identifier: Any other unique identifying number, characteristic or code. Example from Emily's records: Claim number 2 3 0 9 8 9 0 8.

lines.raw: How to remember them.
lines.say: How to remember them.

lines.raw: Think in groups: **who** (name, face, biometrics), **where** (address, small geography), **when** (dates, ages over 89), **how to contact** (phone, fax, email, URL, IP), **numbers** (SSN, record, member, account, licence, vehicle, device) and **anything else unique**.
lines.say: Think in groups: who (name, face, biometrics), where (address, small geography), when (dates, ages over 89), how to contact (phone, fax, email, U R L, I P), numbers (S S N, record, member, account, licence, vehicle, device) and anything else unique.

lines.raw: Not on the list does not mean safe.
lines.say: Not on the list does not mean safe.

lines.raw: A diagnosis code is not an identifier.
lines.say: A diagnosis code is not an identifier.

lines.raw: But a rare diagnosis plus a small town plus an age can still point to one person.
lines.say: But a rare diagnosis plus a small town plus an age can still point to one person.

lines.raw: The list is a minimum, not a guarantee.
lines.say: The list is a minimum, not a guarantee.

lines.raw: Who must follow HIPAA?
lines.say: Who must follow HIPAA?

lines.raw: HIPAA applies to two groups: **covered entities**, the organisations at the centre of healthcare, and **business associates**, the companies they hire to work with PHI.
lines.say: HIPAA applies to two groups: covered entities, the organisations at the centre of healthcare, and business associates, the companies they hire to work with P H I.

lines.raw: Covered entities: the three types.
lines.say: Covered entities: the three types.

lines.raw: **Health plans**. Who: Insurers, HMOs, employer group health plans, Medicare, Medicaid. Emily's example: Emily's PPO plan (TXPPO1000).
lines.say: Health plans. Who: Insurers, H M O's, employer group health plans, Medicare, Medicaid. Emily's example: Emily's P P O plan (T X P P O 1 0 0 0).

lines.raw: **Healthcare providers**. Who: Doctors, hospitals, pharmacies, labs, if they send standard electronic transactions such as claims. Emily's example: Dr. Patel, Lakeside General Hospital.
lines.say: Healthcare providers. Who: Doctors, hospitals, pharmacies, labs, if they send standard electronic transactions such as claims. Emily's example: Doctor Patel, Lakeside General Hospital.

lines.raw: **Healthcare clearinghouses**. Who: Companies that convert claims between formats and route them to payers. Emily's example: The clearinghouse that turns Dr. Patel's billing system output into an 837P.
lines.say: Healthcare clearinghouses. Who: Companies that convert claims between formats and route them to payers. Emily's example: The clearinghouse that turns Doctor Patel's billing system output into an 8 3 7 P.

lines.raw: Business associate (BA).
lines.say: Business associate (B A).

lines.raw: A person or company that does work **for** a covered entity and needs PHI to do it.
lines.say: A person or company that does work for a covered entity and needs P H I to do it.

lines.raw: Examples: claims processors, billing and coding companies, cloud hosting, data analytics firms, lawyers and auditors who see PHI.
lines.say: Examples: claims processors, billing and coding companies, cloud hosting, data analytics firms, lawyers and auditors who see P H I.

lines.raw: Subcontractor.
lines.say: Subcontractor.

lines.raw: A company hired by a business associate that also touches PHI.
lines.say: A company hired by a business associate that also touches P H I.

lines.raw: It is treated as a business associate too, so the duties flow all the way down the chain.
lines.say: It is treated as a business associate too, so the duties flow all the way down the chain.

lines.raw: BAA (Business Associate Agreement).
lines.say: B A A (Business Associate Agreement).

lines.raw: The contract a covered entity must sign with each business associate before sharing PHI.
lines.say: The contract a covered entity must sign with each business associate before sharing P H I.

lines.raw: It says what the BA may do with the PHI, how it must protect it, and that it must report breaches.
lines.say: It says what the B A may do with the P H I, how it must protect it, and that it must report breaches.

lines.raw: Covered entity.
lines.say: Covered entity.

lines.raw: Emily's health plan holds her claims.
lines.say: Emily's health plan holds her claims.

lines.raw: BAA signed.
lines.say: B A A signed.

lines.raw: The plan hires a US analytics company and signs a BAA with it.
lines.say: The plan hires a U S analytics company and signs a B A A with it.

lines.raw: Subcontractor BAA.
lines.say: Subcontractor B A A.

lines.raw: The analytics company hires a data team in Kathmandu and signs a BAA (or similar contract) with them.
lines.say: The analytics company hires a data team in Kathmandu and signs a B A A (or similar contract) with them.

lines.raw: Same rules, all the way down.
lines.say: Same rules, all the way down.

lines.raw: The Kathmandu team must protect Emily's data just as the plan would.
lines.say: The Kathmandu team must protect Emily's data just as the plan would.

lines.raw: The same idea in Nepal.
lines.say: The same idea in Nepal.

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: Ram's insurer may use a third-party company to check hospital bills.
lines.say: Ram's insurer may use a third-party company to check hospital bills.

lines.raw: Ram's diagnosis passes to that company.
lines.say: Ram's diagnosis passes to that company.

lines.raw: In Nepal, how that company must protect it depends mostly on its contract and general privacy law.
lines.say: In Nepal, how that company must protect it depends mostly on its contract and general privacy law.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: Sita's SSF-listed hospital shares her records with SSF for payment.
lines.say: Sita's S S F listed hospital shares her records with S S F for payment.

lines.raw: You can think of SSF as a "health plan" and the hospital as a "provider".
lines.say: You can think of S S F as a "health plan" and the hospital as a "provider".

lines.raw: In US terms, both would be covered entities.
lines.say: In U S terms, both would be covered entities.

lines.raw: In the US: Who is NOT covered by HIPAA.
lines.say: In the U S: Who is N O T covered by HIPAA.

lines.raw: Emily's **employer** acting as an employer (for example, a sick note in her HR file).
lines.say: Emily's employer acting as an employer (for example, a sick note in her H R file).

lines.raw: The employer's **health plan** is covered, but HR is not.
lines.say: The employer's health plan is covered, but H R is not.

lines.raw: A **fitness app** or smartwatch company that Emily signs up for directly.
lines.say: A fitness app or smartwatch company that Emily signs up for directly.

lines.raw: **Life insurance** companies.
lines.say: Life insurance companies.

lines.raw: Emily herself: she can share her own health information with anyone she likes.
lines.say: Emily herself: she can share her own health information with anyone she likes.

lines.raw: Other laws may still protect this data, but HIPAA itself does not.
lines.say: Other laws may still protect this data, but HIPAA itself does not.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: PHI = health or payment information + something that identifies the person, held by a covered entity or BA.
lines.say: P H I = health or payment information and something that identifies the person, held by a covered entity or B A.

lines.raw: HIPAA lists 18 identifiers, including names, small geography, dates (except year), contact details, ID numbers, photos and any other unique code.
lines.say: HIPAA lists 18 identifiers, including names, small geography, dates (except year), contact details, I D numbers, photos and any other unique code.

lines.raw: Covered entities: health plans, healthcare providers that bill electronically, and clearinghouses.
lines.say: Covered entities: health plans, healthcare providers that bill electronically, and clearinghouses.

lines.raw: Business associates work with PHI on their behalf and must sign a BAA.
lines.say: Business associates work with P H I on their behalf and must sign a B A A.

lines.raw: Subcontractors are business associates too.
lines.say: Subcontractors are business associates too.
